text:
alex: Quick heads-up — the load test yesterday flagged a 20% tail-latency regression on A100 vs our baseline. Can we regroup on environment parity?
maria: Ugh. Do we know if it's driver/CUDA-related or something in the container image?
ryan: My first guess is CUDA/cuDNN mismatch + different NCCL flags. The repro VM uses cuda-11.8 but our perf harness uses 12.1 on prod nodes.
jiao: Also saw noise from KV cache warmup. If replay harness doesn't pre-warm KV entries the first 50 requests spike a lot. That skews p95.
alex: Good point — we need apples-to-apples: GPU model, driver, CUDA, kernel flags, container runtime, and the exact model binary + kernels.
perf-bot: [auto] loadtest:run finished 1769814000 — p50 24ms, p95 310ms, error_rate 0.3% 
ryan: Can we add a checklist to the harness that verifies: `nvidia-smi --query`, `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`, `uname -r`, `docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}'`?
maria: Yes. Also verify `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` are consistent. Small env differences can flip kernel selection heuristics.
jiao: Suggestion: two-mode runs — (1) strict-parity replay using recorded traces and identical env; (2) synthetic steady-state to stress batching heuristics. Compare diffs.
alex: Agreed. For strict-parity we should capture the following at trace time: GPU PCI ID, driver version, kernel boot args (`cat /proc/cmdline`), container image digest, and the exact shared object hashes for inference runtime.
ryan: We should also snapshot nvcc/cuda toolkit version and the output of `ldd libinference.so` — kernel selection depends on which kernels are present at runtime.
maria: On batching: replay harness emits request timestamps; but the batcher in-house uses continuous batching with a 4ms aggregation window. We need to make sure replay preserves inter-arrival distribution, not just QPS.
alex: Right — synthetic poisson arrivals hide microburst behavior. Replayer should support replaying original timestamps and an option to compress/stretch time.
ryan: For KV cache, add a pre-warm mode that replays prefix tokens to populate KV per model instance. We must run with and without pre-warm to quantify impact.
jiao: Can we add a small profiling hook to capture kernel selection logs? e.g., set INFERENCE_DEBUG=1 and capture first 500ms of logs for each run.
perf-bot: [auto] parity-check added tag `env-mismatch` to run 1769814000 — collected driver+cuda manifests.
sre-ops: Note: kernel flags that matter — `transparent_hugepage`, `rcu_nocbs`, and `irqbalance` policies. We'll pin them the same on perf and prod.
maria: Also ensure GPU power cap and persistence-daemon state are identical. Those influenced clock gating on one cluster.
alex: Action items: (@maria) add env snapshot to harness; (@ryan) implement pre-warm option and arrival-time replay; (@jiao) add kernel-selection log capture; (@sre-ops) freeze sysctl/kernel flags and GPU power cap for test pool.
maria: I'll open a short PR with the snapshot script and attach expected manifest JSON.
ryan: I'll push a replay-mode flag to the harness and add a small tool to convert recorded traces into compressed/replayed variants.
jiao: I'll add a debug flag that saves the kernel chooser output and the per-batch kernel id mapping. Keep logs compact.
sre-ops: I'll schedule a reserved A100 pool with cuda-11.8 and a matching container image digest for the parity run.
alex: Thanks all. Plan to run strict-parity + synthetic steady-state tomorrow 09:00 PT. Post results in this thread, small tables or snippets ok. :eyes:
maria: noted — will include manifest and `docker inspect --format '{{.Image}}'` output in results.
ryan: If p95 still diverges, we'll bisect by flipping driver/CUDA then kernel flags. Prefer to change one axis at a time.
jiao: Quick tip — include a run with `--batcher-bypass` to measure pure single-request kernel latency baseline. Helps isolate batching vs kernel perf.
alex: Perfect. If anyone finds a quick reproduce, ping me. Otherwise we'll reconvene after the runs. :thumbsup:
